item.title: Keeping documentation in step with the code
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: Ze generates public reference from its code and records, with links to the decisions behind them. Operators and future AI sessions can use the same maintained account of the system.

item.title: AI coding has not had its Rails moment
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: AI coding needs shared conventions for connecting requirements and design decisions to their implementation, and for keeping those relationships current.

item.title: The repository is half the AI harness
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: Ze's development rules define what an AI agent must achieve and how to check the result, including the qualities a working demonstration can leave untested.

item.title: The proof is the expensive part
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: Ze aims to meet every applicable mandatory RFC requirement. Interoperability labs and tests tied to the RFC text help establish what the running router does and which claims remain unverified.

item.title: How Ze reuses memory for BGP UPDATEs
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: From the Amiga demo scene to BGP UPDATEs, earlier experience informs how Ze reuses memory and avoids unnecessary allocation in Go.

item.title: AI slop is human slop
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: AI often writes better code than I would, and far more tests per feature. I judge that code by what it does and the evidence behind it, and remain responsible for what Ze releases.
